$comment: Baseline allowlist for scripts/verify. Public output must stay byte-identical during the current monorepo-migration phase — any pre-existing issue found here is NOT fixed by the verifier or by this file, only documented so CI stays green today. The matching key is (check, code, route, detail) — `detail` is optional (e.g. the exact duplicated title/description text) and an entry that omits it matches only an issue that itself has no `detail`, so a NEW, different collision on the same route is never silently hidden behind an old entry. Any issue whose key doesn't match an entry here still fails the build. Every entry needs a self-contained `reason` (don't reference other entries or files outside this repo). Remove an entry once the underlying issue is actually fixed — a run that never re-triggers it is reported as 'stale': index.mjs only prints this (informational), but secrets-scan.mjs fails the run on it.

entries.reason: Pre-existing content data: packages/content/src/data/projects.ts has two distinct real projects in Calpe (slugs "hormigon-impreso-calpe" and "hormigon-impreso-calpe-2") whose title-building fields produce the exact same generated <title>. Public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase, so not fixed here; belongs in a content-data task (disambiguate the title, e.g. by district). `detail` pins this entry to that exact generated title text — a future, different title collision on this same route is a new issue, not this one.

Pre-existing content data bug in packages/content/src/data/projects.ts: the project with slug "hormigon-pulido-alicante" has `town: 'Benissa'` (a different real job there, district "Montemar la Viña" vs. the other Benissa project's "Monte Mar"), so its generated title/description collide with the actual "hormigon-pulido-benissa" project. The "-alicante" slug itself is a public URL (a WordPress-era 301 in next.config.ts targets it), so it can't just be renamed to match the town — this needs a real content-data fix (retitle using the district, not the town), done separately; not fixed here since public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase. `detail` pins this entry to that exact generated title text — a future, different title collision on this same route is a new issue, not this one.
